# Job Chapter 23 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 424v–425r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_023_page_001.jpg, JOB_023_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "Even today my complaint is bitter; my hand is heavy despite my groaning.

**3** Oh, that I knew where I might find him, that I might come to his dwelling place!

**4** I would lay my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.

**5** I would learn the words with which he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.

**6** Would he contend with me by his great power? No, he would give heed to me.

**7** There an upright man could reason with him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.

**8** Behold, I go forward, but he is not there, and backward, but I cannot perceive him;

**9** on the left when he is working, I cannot behold him; he turns to the right, but I cannot see him.

**10** But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I shall come forth as gold.

**11** My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept his way and have not turned aside.

**12** I have not departed from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.

**13** But he stands alone, and who can turn him back? What his soul desires, that he does.

**14** For he will complete what he has decreed for me, and many such things are in his mind.

**15** Therefore I am dismayed at his presence; when I consider, I am in dread of him.

**16** God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has dismayed me;

**17** yet I am not silenced by the darkness, nor by the thick darkness that covers my face."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**v.2 — "my hand is heavy despite my groaning":** Following the Qere/Ketiv tradition — the Ketiv reads *yadi* ("my hand"), while many interpreters emend to *yado* ("his hand"). LOGOS follows the MT consonantal text while acknowledging the difficulty.

**v.7 — "delivered forever from my judge":** Job's confidence that a fair hearing would result in acquittal. The irony is exquisite — Job wants a trial, but he cannot even locate the courtroom.

**v.10 — "come forth as gold":** This is the high-water mark of Job's faith amid suffering. The refining metaphor will be echoed in Malachi 3:3 and 1 Peter 1:7.

**v.13 — "he stands alone":** God's utter sovereignty is simultaneously Job's hope (v.10) and his terror (vv.15-16). The theological tension is deliberately unresolved.

*— LOGOS*
